newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen firm but rises limited in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen firm but rises limited in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is likely to maintain its bullish tone against the yen and the mark during Asian trading time on Friday, but rises may be limited as a lack of market-moving factors is expected to keep it range-bound, dealers said.
Offers from exporters and interbank traders above 116 yen are likely to cap the dollar's gains near 116.50 yen, while support is seen near 115.70/80 yen.
Dealers said the market will continue to focus on moves in European currencies, while the dollar/yen may remain sidelined.

The U.S. currency soared to a high of 1.8400 marks in European trade on Thursday as players expressed relief that the German central bank had not switched from a fixed to a variable repo rate as some had speculated. The Bundesbank's decision to stick with a fixed rate repo is a sign to many traders that German officials are willing to live with a weak mark.
Tokyo dealers said the greenback is expected to remain strong against the mark but may wait until European trading time later in the day to test its upside towards 1.84 marks.
"I think it is difficult to have another upside probe to 1.84 marks during Tokyo trading time," a bank dealer said.

A city bank dealer said the dollar's downside is becoming solid near 115 yen and the greenback is set to edge up gradually to test 116.50 yen. "As the Bundesbank did not do anything (with its monetary policy), the fact that the dollar is the strongest currency around has not changed," he added. The first bank dealer, however, said Japanese city banks are seen having offers above 116 yen, weighing on the dollar.

Overnight, the dollar hit a high of 1.51 Swiss francs, its highest level since November 1993, while heavy sales of Swiss francs for marks by U.S. funds and banks pushed the mark/Swiss rate up to 0.8215 from a low of 0.8090.
But the first bank dealer said he does not expect wild fluctuations in the Swiss franc in Tokyo as liquidity in the Swiss franc market is not very high.
